releases.notes: Gemini 1.0 Ultra was unveiled Dec 6, 2023 (blog.google/technology/ai/google-gemini-ai/) but was not itself publicly usable then — only Gemini Pro shipped in Bard/API that day. GPQA was not reported for Ultra in either the announcement or the technical report.

releases.name: Gemini 2.0 Pro Experimental

announcement.title: Gemini 2.0 is now available to everyone
announcement.quote: We’re also releasing an experimental version of Gemini 2.0 Pro, our best model yet for coding performance and complex prompts.

releases.notes: Released only as a free-standing 'Experimental' model (gemini-2.0-pro-exp-02-05) in Google AI Studio, Vertex AI and the Gemini app for Gemini Advanced users — never reached general availability and was superseded by Gemini 2.5 Pro about seven weeks later. Counted here as 'released' per project convention because it was publicly usable (no waitlist), not merely announced. Google did not publish a numeric academic-benchmark table alongside this launch (the post and companion Google for Developers post describe capability only qualitatively); no verifiable official score could be found for this specific checkpoint, so scores are left empty rather than guessed.

The model card's own capability-benchmark table is rendered as an image with no extractable text, so numeric scores here are taken from the launch blog post instead. A more capable 'Gemini 3 Deep Think' mode (HLE 41.0%, GPQA 93.8%, ARC-AGI-2 45.1% with code execution) was announced the same day but rolled out to Google AI Ultra subscribers later; it is treated as a mode of this release rather than a separate flagship.

source.quote: On ARC-AGI-2, a benchmark that evaluates a model’s ability to solve entirely new logic patterns, 3.1 Pro achieved a verified score of 77.1%.

releases.notes: Launched in preview (Gemini API in AI Studio, Gemini CLI, Google Antigravity, Android Studio; Vertex AI and Gemini Enterprise for business; Gemini app and NotebookLM for consumers) — not yet GA at launch, per the post's own 'before we make it generally available soon'. Counted as released per project convention since it was immediately publicly usable, mirroring the treatment of Gemini 2.0/2.5 Pro Experimental. The launch post itself gives only the ARC-AGI-2 number; the model card's fuller benchmark comparison is an image, and third-party-reported figures for GPQA Diamond (~94.3%) and other benchmarks could not be traced to a quotable, verbatim official Google statement, so they are omitted rather than guessed.

releases.name: Gemini 3.5 Pro

announcement.title: Google releases three new Gemini models — but no 3.5 Pro
announcement.quote: Google DeepMind product lead Logan Kilpatrick said Tuesday that the company is currently testing Gemini 3.5 Pro with partners and hopes to “land soon.”

releases.notes: Teased at Google I/O (May 19, 2026) alongside the Gemini 3.5 Flash launch, with Google saying Pro was 'already being used internally' and would roll out 'next month'. As of this writing (Sep 7, 2026) it has missed at least three targets (June, mid-July, early August 2026); Bloomberg reported (Jul 16, 2026) that its coding performance was falling short of Google's internal goals. No model ID, pricing or firm launch date has been published, so no expected_window is recorded. Still unreleased and untested, hence no scores.

releases.name: Gemini 4

announcement.title: Google releases three new Gemini models — but no 3.5 Pro
announcement.quote: He also noted that the team has started its most ambitious pre-training run yet for Gemini 4.

releases.notes: Confirmed by Google DeepMind product lead Logan Kilpatrick (via X, reported by TechCrunch) on Jul 21, 2026: pre-training has begun, described by Sundar Pichai on the Q2 2026 earnings call (Jul 23) as needing to be 'significantly larger' than Gemini 3 to compete with rivals, with coding and autonomous agents named as priorities. 'Gemini 4' is the working/rumored name; no architecture, benchmark, price, access plan or release window has been disclosed, so date_precision is 'day' only for the announcement itself and no expected_window is recorded.
